sentences: The bill would shut down the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA).
It would repeal the 2011 Act that created ARENA and gave it funding and governance rules.
The changes would start when the bill becomes law, and the Industry Department would take over ARENA's unfinished business.
changes: Closes the Australian Renewable Energy Agency.
Repeals the Australian Renewable Energy Agency Act 2011.
Transfers ARENA's commitments, assets and liabilities to the Commonwealth Minister and Department of Industry.
Cancels any undecided applications for financial assistance from ARENA.
summary.affected: The Australian Renewable Energy Agency, the Commonwealth Minister, the Department of Industry, and applicants for ARENA financial assistance.

divisions.question: Australian Renewable Energy Agency (Repeal) Bill 2014 — Second Reading — Criticise abolition of ARENA
Australian Renewable Energy Agency (Repeal) Bill 2014 - Second Reading - Read a second time

speeches.speaker: Ian Macfarlane
speeches.brief: Introduced a bill to repeal the Australian Renewable Energy Agency Act and transfer its functions to the department, saying the change would deliver savings of almost $1.3 billion while the existing $1 billion in taxpayer-funded ARENA projects, including a $166 million grant for the AGL solar project at Nyngan and Broken Hill, would continue.

speeches.speaker: Matt Thistlethwaite
speeches.brief: Opposed the bill to repeal the Australian Renewable Energy Agency, saying it had funded nearly 200 renewable energy projects with 70 per cent of funding going to rural and regional Australia, and said Labor's policies had grown rooftop solar households from 7,400 to almost 1.2 million.

speeches.speaker: Bob Baldwin
speeches.brief: Supported transferring ARENA's functions to the Department of Industry, saying the bill would achieve $1.3 billion in budget savings by returning uncommitted funding, highlighted $21.5 million just announced for 12 new solar research projects at the University of New South Wales, and criticised Labor's Green Loans program, which cost an average of $100,000 for each $1,000 loan issued.

speeches.speaker: Kelvin Thomson
speeches.brief: Opposed the repeal of the Australian Renewable Energy Agency, saying it currently supports more than 190 renewable energy projects backed by more than $1.5 billion in private investment, noted renewable energy jobs tripled to more than 24,000 and solar households grew from about 7,000 to over one million under Labor, and cited modelling showing coal generators could gain an extra $25 billion in profit if the renewable energy target were scrapped.

speeches.speaker: Steve Irons
speeches.brief: Supported the government's fiscal reform including the ARENA repeal, warning deficits could rise to $667 billion without action, said Labor delivered $191 billion in deficits over its first five budgets, and cited the National Commission of Audit's finding that unchanged spending would mean continuing deficits for 16 years to 2023-24.

speeches.speaker: Steve Irons
speeches.brief: Continued supporting the ARENA repeal, saying it would save almost $1.3 billion in uncommitted funding while honouring already committed projects, and criticised mismanagement under Labor, citing the Oceanlinx wave energy demonstrator, which sank in South Australia taking nearly $4 million in taxpayer funding with it, and the failed Petratherm hot rocks project, which lost a further $4.2 million.

speeches.speaker: Pat Conroy
speeches.brief: Opposed the ARENA repeal, warning it threatens 24,000 renewable energy jobs and $18 billion in future investment, and said large-scale renewable energy investment collapsed from $2.7 billion in 2013 to just $40 million in the first half of 2014, the lowest level in 14 years, and cited the Garnaut report's warning of a 98 per cent reduction in Murray-Darling farming if climate change is not addressed.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Laming
speeches.brief: Supported repealing ARENA, arguing the government should focus on outcomes rather than maintaining a separate authority, and said Australia's economic mess inherited from Labor required abolishing agencies that duplicated the work departments should do.

speeches.speaker: Jim Chalmers
speeches.brief: Opposed the ARENA repeal bill, citing solar uptake of 42 per cent of households in his Rankin electorate compared with a 22 per cent national average, and warned that abolishing ARENA would cost jobs in the renewable energy sector, particularly in rural areas.

speeches.speaker: Paul Fletcher
speeches.brief: Supported repealing ARENA as a rationalisation, not a rejection of renewable energy, citing $667 billion in projected gross debt and $123 billion in cumulative deficits left by the previous government, and said $1.3 billion in uncommitted ARENA funds could be recovered.

speeches.speaker: Ken O'Dowd
speeches.brief: Supported repealing ARENA, defending coal-fired power in his Flynn electorate, and said the government would still fund around 200 ARENA projects worth over $1 billion nationally while achieving $1.3 billion in budget savings from the repeal.

speeches.speaker: Lisa Chesters
speeches.brief: Opposed the ARENA repeal, citing renewable energy jobs at Hofmann Engineering in her Bendigo electorate and saying a Clean Technology Investment Program grant helped MSD Animal Health Australia cut carbon emissions by 22 per cent and save about $44,000 a year on electricity.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: Supported the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (Repeal) Bill 2014, forecasting savings of almost $1.3 billion, and recalled the previous coalition government paying off $96 billion of Labor debt while also saving $50 billion in interest and banking a further $50 billion, noting Labor's last budget surplus was in 1989.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: Argued for repealing the Australian Renewable Energy Agency to save $1.3 billion in the budget, questioned the value of a $22 billion subsidy under the renewable energy target, and raised Australia's fuel security with only seven days supply in the chain.

speeches.speaker: Mark Dreyfus
speeches.brief: Argued against abolishing the Australian Renewable Energy Agency, noting it supports more than 190 projects and has drawn over $1.5 billion in private investment, and accused the government of repeatedly promising before elections to keep the renewable energy target unchanged.

speeches.speaker: Sharon Claydon
speeches.brief: Opposed repealing the Australian Renewable Energy Agency, highlighting 17 ARENA-backed solar projects worth almost $60 million in her Newcastle electorate led by the CSIRO, and warned that government cuts to CSIRO have already meant more than 700 job losses.

speeches.speaker: Stephen Jones
speeches.brief: Argued against the Australian Renewable Energy Agency's abolition, noting it was funded with about $2.5 billion and leverages 1.8 times private investment, and cited a $2.2 million ARENA grant to BlueScope in his electorate for a solar Colorbond roofing system.

speeches.speaker: Gai Brodtmann
speeches.brief: Warned against abolishing the Australian Renewable Energy Agency, describing a $3 million CSIRO-led solar forecasting project in the ACT worth $7.6 million in total, and cited a Newspoll finding that 98 per cent of Australians support renewable energy.

speeches.speaker: Laurie Ferguson
speeches.brief: Opposed repealing the Australian Renewable Energy Agency, quoting economist Nicholas Stern on the risks of delaying climate action and the International Energy Agency's finding that renewables supplied 22 per cent of world electricity, and cited 1.2 million Australian households with solar.

speeches.speaker: Jill Hall
speeches.brief: Condemned the government's plan to abolish the Australian Renewable Energy Agency, noting it has invested $1 billion and leveraged $1.8 billion from industry, and cited 4,885 solar homes in her Shortland electorate generating 12.2 megawatts of clean energy.

speeches.speaker: Tony Zappia
speeches.brief: Accused the government of breaking a pre-election pledge to keep the Australian Renewable Energy Agency, quoting the Environment Minister's promise to retain it, and cited Tindo Solar, a solar panel manufacturer in his Makin electorate, warning that scrapping renewable schemes would cost jobs there.

speeches.speaker: Melissa Parke
speeches.brief: Argued against abolishing the Australian Renewable Energy Agency, citing $940 million invested and $1.8 billion in private capital it has mobilised, and highlighted the Carnegie Wave Energy project in her Fremantle electorate, which former Japanese Prime Minister Naoto Kan visited.

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Defended the bill to abolish the Australian Renewable Energy Agency to save almost $1.3 billion, citing a failed Oceanlinx wave energy device that received nearly $4 million in grants and a $66.46 million grant to Ocean Power Technologies' scrapped Portland wave project as examples of wasted funding.
